Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36616: test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted

b469ff8fddb6594b69d564cca436b7baa8ed99bb test: keep noban_tx_relay config after node is restarted (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  When a node restarts with extra_args it loses its original extra_args, so the `-whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` set by `noban_tx_relay` is lost and the node falls back to the normal tx relay delays.

  This changes `noban_tx_relay` to set `whitelist=noban,in,out@127.0.0.1` in `extra_confs` instead, so it is kept across restarts.

  This speeds up some tests (running locally `build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j=18 --randomseed=1`):

  mempool_ephemeral_dust.py 49s -> 18s
  mempool_accept_wtxid.py 17s ->  6s
  wallet_fundrawtransaction.py 11s -> 7s

  Accumulated 1152s -> 1110s
  Wall 80s -> 75s

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36581: subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows

cf30d0a4123bb4237495f04e723ce9f706c2edf2 subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  `Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

  `CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

  This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

  _edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36465: Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests

5a4cd70547096af6247167d8dde6145a1b548642 Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests (benthecarman)

Pull request description:

  VerifyScript runs a P2SH scriptPubKey on the stack the scriptSig leaves before handling the redeemScript. The 20-byte push in HASH160 <20> EQUAL adds one item, so a scriptSig that leaves 1,000 items fails with STACK_SIZE, while 999 items is valid.

  An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.

  Add 999 and 1,000 item cases with P2SH and WITNESS, and the 1,000 item case with no flags, which fails the same way because the scriptPubKey always runs. Also add the same boundary during redeemScript evaluation, where the restored stack plus the redeemScript's pushes reach 1,000 and 1,001 items.

  The same case is added as a feature_taproot spender in #36455, so its dump can be added to the script assets (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297).

  These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36453: util, cli: name the Sock wait timeout cap and use it for -rpcclienttimeout=0

d22d3565128828e158c6684a1b5bf1a7f2454c80 util, cli: name the Sock wait timeout cap and use it for -rpcclienttimeout=0 (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  Follow-up to #36340, addressing the review comments from pinheadmz and winterrdog there.

  #36340 capped the `Sock::Wait`/`WaitMany` timeout at `INT_MAX` milliseconds (about 24.8 days) inside `WaitMany`. This moves that value to a named constant, `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and mentions the cap in the doxygen comments of `Wait()` and `WaitMany()`, since it applies to every caller and not only to `bitcoin-cli`. The constant is a whole number of seconds (2147483 s), so `bitcoin-cli`, which works in seconds, uses exactly the same value as `Sock`.

  `bitcoin-cli` still turned `-rpcclienttimeout=0` into a 5 year timeout. The timeout is applied to each wait for the socket, and each wait is now capped, so in practice `0` already means "give up after about 24.8 days without data". The 5 year value is replaced with `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and the help text now says that 0 is the longest supported timeout (about 24 days) instead of no timeout.

  There is no behaviour change. `sock_tests`, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` (including the `-rpcclienttimeout=0` call added in #36340) and `interface_rpc.py` pass on macOS.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36449: addrman: use uniform sampling inside buckets

5aaaf7b8d1ed72b7ab9eee117204f4c4346eb235 test: check network filtering and uniformity of addrman Select (Pieter Wuille)
9a0e095c687d7e139a9571883296cd9321e5beeb addrman: use uniform sampling inside buckets (Pieter Wuille)

Pull request description:

  The current way we sample from addresses within a bucket in addrman is randomized, but not perfectly random. It uses a linear scan, starting at a random position (out of the 64 positions in a bucket). This means that if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).

  Make this search perfectly uniform, regardless of distribution of addresses within the bucket, by first copying all non-empty positions to a temporary array, and then selecting uniformly randomly from that array.

  Suggested by Crypt-iQ. Also pointed out earlier by mzumsande in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23140#discussion_r733084509.

Pull request description:

  Clarify the message in case of assertion failures. Additionally unify the behavior of `NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE` w.r.t. abort handling.

  Motivation: This was discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34844#discussion_r3303436384

  The error message generated by `Assert`, `Assume`, and `CHECK_NONFATAL` contains the failing assertion condition text, but it's unclear whether that's the failed expectation or the actual case.

  For example,
  `"Internal bug detected: pindex != nullptr"`
  in fact means that what happened was `pindex == nullptr`.

  Clarify the situation, by inserting "\`%s\` check failed".

  The above example is now:
  ``"Internal bug detected: `pindex != nullptr` check failed"``
  which is more unambiguous.

  Additionally, change `NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE` to behave like `CHECK_NONFATAL`, and honor the special abort setting (`G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`).

  The test now checks both sides on node2 with `mempool_only=false`: it  succeeds while the spends are still in the mempool, and raises the error once they are mined.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36559: test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

2f7622e3f6f7ef431a7d5ec522958da62f33cec4 test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex (Kevin Ravensberg)

Pull request description:

  `feature_anchors.py` builds the expected `anchors.dat` substring from each peer's port with `hex(port)[2:]`, which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit short and `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` fails.

  This only shows up with a non-default port range, for example when avoiding local listeners:

  ```
  TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py
  ```

  fails on master with `AssertionError` at the `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` line and passes with this change; the default range still passes.

  ---
  Disclosure: AI (Claude Fable 5.1) was used to find this issue and to draft this PR.

f64d33672fe1488b49254a634cbecfd9ce4ca179 wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `bitcoin-wallet create` exits with status 0 even when the wallet couldn't be created:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create   # first time, ok
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create
  Failed to create database path '.../regtest/wallets/w1'. Database already exists.
  $ echo $?
  0
  ```

  In `ExecuteWalletToolFunc` the `create` branch only does something when `MakeWallet` succeeds and then falls through to `return true`. The other commands (`info`, `dump`, `createfromdump`) all return false on failure. So scripts that check the exit code think the wallet was created.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36339: wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions

9cff82fd5b15bc2aa2c7778b61212876433a8219 wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `listtransactions` adds `count` and `skip` as `int`. Each one is checked to be non-negative, but their sum can still go past INT_MAX:

  ```
  bitcoin-cli -regtest listtransactions "*" 2147483647 1
  ```

  On master this crashes the node. The overflowed sum is negative, so the loop stops after the first entry. The clamp after the loop overflows the same way and doesn't fix `nCount`, so `push_backV` gets an iterator range about 2^31 elements before `rend()`. UBSan reports `signed integer overflow: 1 + 2147483647` at transactions.cpp:584, and ASan then reports a BUS error in `UniValue::push_backV`.

  This parses `count` and `skip` as `uint32_t` through `self.Arg` (which also handles the defaults and rejects negative values, so the manual checks go away) and adds them up in 64 bits, where the sum can't overflow. The functional test calls `listtransactions` with count + skip above INT_MAX and up to UINT32_MAX and checks the results match a normal-sized request. It times out on master (the node crashes) and passes with the fix. I also ran it on an ASan/UBSan build.

  `listrawtransactions` counts differently and isn't affected.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36368: bitcoin-tx: reject in and outscript arguments with too many separators

2fef1db4f88a02efd666da41bc3641345940669d bitcoin-tx: reject in and outscript arguments with too many separators (Bruce0X)

Pull request description:

  `outscript=VALUE:SCRIPT[:FLAGS]` only reads the flags when there are exactly three fields (bitcoin-tx.cpp:482). With a trailing or extra `:` the flags are silently dropped:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S nversion=1
  010000000001000000000000000017a91471ed53322d470bb96657deb786b94f97dd46fb158700000000  # P2SH, as requested
  $ bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S: nversion=1
  0100000000010000000000000000017500000000  # bare OP_DROP output, exit code 0
  ```

  So a typo gives a transaction paying to the raw script instead of the P2SH/P2WSH wrapper, with no error. `outpubkey` and `outaddr` already reject extra fields with "TX output missing or too many separators".

  This rejects `outscript` arguments with more than three fields, and `in=TXID:VOUT[:SEQUENCE_NUMBER]` arguments with more than three fields (which were accepted the same way), both with a general "Invalid format, expected ..." error. `bitcoin-util-test.json` gets a case for each; they fail on master (exit code 0) and pass with the fix, and `tool_utils.py` passes.

  AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

commit.message:
test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

The test builds the expected anchors.dat substring from the peer's port
with hex(port)[2:], which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as
two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit
short and the assertion fails:

    TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py

Format the port as four hex digits instead.

util, cli: name the Sock wait timeout cap and use it for -rpcclienttimeout=0

#36340 capped the timeout of Sock::Wait/WaitMany at INT_MAX milliseconds
(about 24.8 days) inside WaitMany. Move the value to a named constant,
Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT, and mention the cap in the Wait() and WaitMany()
docs, since it applies to every caller. The constant is a whole number
of seconds (2147483 s), so callers that work in seconds use exactly the
same value.

bitcoin-cli turned -rpcclienttimeout=0 into a 5 year timeout, which is
now capped to the same value on every wait, so "5 years" no longer
describes what happens. Use Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT directly, and say in
the help text that 0 means the longest supported timeout (about 24 days)
instead of no timeout.

No behaviour change.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36535: policy: sum package weight in int64_t

faaabe4454c14537e9f23bd349d43d7233df14fe policy: sum package weight in int64_t (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `IsWellFormedPackage` sums the package weight with `std::accumulate` starting from a plain `0`, so the running total is an `int`. A package heavier than `INT_MAX` would wrap and could pass the `MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT` check. No package that large reaches this check today, since RPC request bodies are capped at 32 MiB and P2P messages at 4 MB, so this is defense in depth. It picks up the one-line fix from #35473, which was closed with an invitation to do so.

  I start the sum from `int64_t{0}`, as the vsize sum in `validation.cpp` already does. I did not add a test, since the one on #35473 was turned down. I checked the fix locally with a throwaway test that puts one transaction of 88M weight into a package 25 times: before the fix the package is rejected as `package-contains-duplicates`, after it as `package-too-large`.

common: drop locale setting hack

environments locale was invalid. Boost.Filesystem has been removed, and

calls `setlocale`).

Qt calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` on startup, and falls back to C.UTF-8
if the locale isn't UTF-8.

translation on all systems, also in CI. Before, they ran in English in

commit.message:
policy: sum package weight in int64_t

std::accumulate keeps its running total in the type of its initial
value. IsWellFormedPackage passed a plain 0, so the package weight was
summed in an int, even though the lambda and the result are int64_t.
A package heavier than INT_MAX would wrap and could pass the
MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT check. No such package reaches this check today:
RPC request bodies and P2P messages are far smaller.

Start the sum from int64_t{0}, as the vsize sum in validation.cpp
already does.

Pull request description:

  A few of our longer-running tests have some unnecessary waits and timeouts in them. Reduce or replace them to shorten test times:

  - in `p2p_node_network_limited` replace the expected sync timeout with header/ping barriers and a bounded negative check. At CI timeout factor 40, saves roughly 195 seconds per transport.

  The timeout changes alone save approximately eight minutes of accumulated test-worker time on CI jobs running both transports and IPC mining. Wall-clock savings depend on parallel scheduling, CPU etc.

commit.message:
test: check network filtering and uniformity of addrman Select

Add a unit test that places IPv4 and IPv6 addresses at chosen positions
within a single new bucket, and verifies (using a chi-square test) that
Select() returns only entries matching the requested networks, each with
equal probability.

Also make the addrman fuzz target assert that Select() returns an address
if and only if there are entries matching the filters, and that the
returned address matches the network filter, if one is provided.

fuzz: fix stale comments in http_request

A completed request is no longer always handed back to a worker; it stays
in m_req when the send buffer is full.

Also drop the pre-existing comment/note about what ReadBody() returned before the libevent
replacement.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Zipkin <pinheadmz@pm.me>

cmpctblock: log: Print sizes of all tx types and prefill redundancies

At block reconstruction time, log the counts and sizes of prefilled
transactions, transactions pulled from the mempool, transactions from
the extrapool, and missing transactions that were acquired via
`GETBLOCKTXN`.

Also log the count and size of prefilled transactions that were
redundant and their source (mempool or extrapool).
